title: Two origin stories for the brain
facts: A Stanford-led study found that the forebrain and midbrain develop from a different early cell population than the hindbrain.
The findings suggest two distinct developmental starting points for these brain regions, rather than a single starting point.
Using this distinction, the researchers grew functional human hindbrain motor neurons in the laboratory.
cautions: Present this as a research finding, not settled consensus. It does not mean a person has two independent minds or personalities. Do not claim the research has cured a disease.

title: Microduck: a robot that learns to move
facts: Microduck is a small, duck-shaped walking robot, about 25 centimetres tall, with an articulated beak that can pick up objects.
Developers can train its movements in a physics simulation and then run those learned behaviours on the physical robot.
Its learned behaviours include walking, getting back up after common falls, and roller-skating with skates fitted.
cautions: This is a programmable robot, not a living or conscious animal. Do not imply it instantly learns arbitrary tricks from spoken commands or can perform general household chores. Its software is open source; do not claim its hardware is open source.

title: Attention Is All You Need — original paper
facts: Attention Is All You Need is the 2017 paper that introduced the Transformer neural-network architecture.
Its Transformer uses attention mechanisms without recurrent or convolutional layers.
Self-attention lets the model relate different positions within a sequence, and the paper demonstrated machine translation with more parallel training.
cautions: This is the original research paper, not a beginner tutorial or a new 2026 discovery. Attention existed before this paper; do not claim its authors invented attention itself. Do not imply the model thinks like a human or reads minds.

title: Neural Networks Are Already Clean — Nick Cammarata
facts: Nick Cammarata revisits a famous neuron that responded to both cats and cars, arguing that it detects a shared V-shaped pattern.
He argues that architecture problems and weak analysis tools made some neural networks appear more tangled than they really were.
The essay proposes studying native neurons and circuits directly; Cammarata presents the broader argument as a working hypothesis.
cautions: Attribute the interpretation to Nick Cammarata or frame it as his argument. It is a working hypothesis, not proof that all AI is understood or that AI safety is solved. Do not claim all neurons have one simple meaning or that superposition never occurs.

title: Machines of Loving Grace — Dario Amodei
facts: Dario Amodei sketches an optimistic future in which powerful AI could improve health, reduce poverty, and change work and meaning.
He speculates that, after powerful AI is developed, fifty to one hundred years of biological and medical progress could be compressed into five to ten years.
The essay explicitly presents these possibilities as uncertain guesses, and says an inspiring positive vision matters alongside work on AI risks.
cautions: Always attribute forecasts to Dario Amodei and use could, imagines, or predicts. These are speculative possibilities, not achieved results or guaranteed timelines. The five-to-ten-year forecast begins after powerful AI exists, not from today. Do not promise cures, immortality, or an end to poverty.
